title: Enabling Ubuntu's TPM encryption switches you to a snap kernel that blocks deb kernel packages · bare.systems
excerpt: On Ubuntu, enabling TPM-FDE silently gives you a snap-based system, which can quietly break hardware enablement, like Dell laptop cameras.
content_html:
TL;DR: Rediscovering that on Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, ticking “Use hardware-backed disk encryption” in the installer silently gives you a snap-based system (snap kernel and bootloader, like Ubuntu Core) instead of a normal deb-based one. On a modern laptop, this can breaks hardware enablement, in my case the webcam, with no supported way to fix it or have an equivalent feature set.

I got my hands on a Dell Latitude 7450, certified with Ubuntu 22.04 (this Ubuntu blog post on the certification process is worth a read), and decided to try a newer LTS version. Ubuntu 26.04 was out but really new, so I decided to start with 24.04. I downloaded the ISO, ticked the disk encryption checkbox using TPM (I had to disable third-party drivers for that), and found myself with a system where the camera was not working.

In the past, I never had a flawless experience using Ubuntu on a laptop, but those were from non-certified machines. The Latitude 7450 had Canonical’s blessing, so what was going on? Surprisingly, reinstalling with the same ISO and ticking a different encryption checkbox (LVM with passphrase) makes the camera work out of the box.

Let’s try to figure out what happened.

Discovering the issue in vanilla 24.04

Initially, on my 24.04 installation, most just worked out-of-the-box. Ubuntu installed a meta package oem-somerville-oddish-meta (“Somerville” is Dell’s OEM program, “Oddish” the codename for this laptop, yes like the Pokémon), adding Dell’s apt archive to my sources, so I was confident about compatibility. After verifications the iGPU, Wi-Fi, audio, fingerprint reader and Thunderbolt all worked. It seemed the work Dell did building their Latitude_7450_Latitude_7650_Ubuntu_2204_A01_Recovery_image.iso 22.04 had since moved upstream, good job!

Except…

The camera doesn’t work, and nothing can fix it

The webcam was the obvious omission, with no /dev/video* at all. The hardware was fine (the laptop was new, and lsusb showed the chip). dkms status listed the IPU6 camera modules as registered but never built. Searching the internet, the recipe for this exact problem was: install the pre-built camera modules from Dell’s archive instead of the DKMS ones, add v4l2-relayd, reboot, done. Surprise surprise, it did not install:

$ sudo apt install linux-modules-ipu6-generic ...
 linux-modules-ipu6-6.8.0-111-generic : Depends: linux-image-6.8.0-111-generic but it is not going to be installed

The modules need a kernel image to attach to. Alright, let’s get that kernel image:

$ sudo apt install linux-image-6.8.0-111-generic linux-modules-ipu6-generic ...
 boot-managed-by-snapd : Conflicts: linux-image, grub-efi-amd64, grub-pc,
                                    linux-firmware, shim-signed ...

Oh no.

My kernel is a snap!

I was taken aback, what did boot-managed-by-snapd mean? I knew the word boot, and I knew the word snap, but a snap-managed boot? It was conflicting with linux-image, GRUB, shim, linux-firmware, basically everything Debian-based systems use to boot.

$ cat /proc/cmdline
snapd_recovery_mode=run console=tty1 ...
$ snap list | grep pc-kernel
pc-kernel   6.8.0-110.110   3374   24/stable   canonical✓   kernel
$ dpkg -l | grep linux-image
(no output)
$ ls /boot/efi
ls: cannot access '/boot/efi': No such file or directory

There was no deb kernel, no /boot/efi. My kernel was a snap, and I didn’t know what to make of it. After some research, I learned about Ubuntu Core, actually a pretty cool immutable distro for embedded devices, but this was not what I thought I was installing for my normal laptop use. Having installed Debian and Ubuntu dozens of times, I couldn’t figure out what I’d done differently.

A dead end with the camera on the snap side

Could I get the camera working anyway, staying on the snap kernel? The pre-built modules were there, so that left building them with DKMS. They built fine, but would not load:

$ sudo modprobe intel_ipu6
modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'intel_ipu6': Key was rejected by service

Secure Boot, which TPM-FDE requires, refused unsigned modules. To sign my own I’d need to enroll a key, which changes PCR 7, which is what the TPM is using for decryption. I could recover from that with the recovery key, but the documentation is blunt about the side-effect: “On subsequent boots, you have to continue using your recovery key.” There’s no supported way to reconverge after that. On this kernel, I was hitting a dead end for the camera.

I still didn’t know why the camera was missing in the first place, so I decided to reinstall without TPM encryption, giving me a chance to disable Secure Boot and try again.

Reinstalling: plot twist

I reinstalled from the same ISO, this time choosing plain LUKS with a passphrase instead of TPM encryption. Then, before running any single command on my system, I checked the camera again:

$ ls /dev/video*
*49 entries*

Amazingly, the camera was working. cheese showed my face. I’d done nothing. What had changed?

The first thing I noticed was the kernel. uname -r showed a plain deb HWE kernel, and boot-managed-by-snapd was gone. The snap kernel was gone, good job me! I felt like my dog when I congratulate him: he feels very happy, but I’m pretty sure he doesn’t always know what he’s done.

That sent me back to Canonical’s blog post about the TPM-FDE feature, which describes what the checkbox actually does: “TPM-backed FDE: this will install a classic desktop system that gets its kernel and bootloader assets from snaps. Non TPM-backed FDE: this will install an entirely deb-based classic desktop system.” So one checkbox silently chooses between two architecturally different operating systems. Ubuntu has decided, for better or worse, that TPM encryption requires their snap-managed kernel.

That single difference explained the working camera. On a deb system, oem-somerville-oddish-meta is more than a stub pointing to a remote archive: once it adds the Dell archive, apt finds a higher-versioned package of the same name inside that archive, and that one pulls the HWE kernel and the camera stack. So the entire Latitude 7450 hardware stack works out-of-the-box on 24.04, zero effort required. On snap, it can’t, because the Dell OEM package depends on the linux-image deb, nowhere to be found in a snap environment.

Getting the TPM auto-unlock anyway, without snap

I still wanted the laptop to unlock itself without snap’s arcane machinery. A systemd-cryptenroll route I found online looked right but didn’t work, because Ubuntu’s initramfs uses the older Debian cryptsetup wrapper that silently ignores the TPM option. Fortunately, one of my favorite Linux tools came to the rescue: clevis.

sudo apt install clevis-luks clevis-tpm2 clevis-initramfs
sudo clevis luks bind -d /dev/nvme0n1p3 tpm2 '{"pcr_bank":"sha256","pcr_ids":"7"}'
sudo update-initramfs -u

While I had to wipe the first systemd-cryptenroll attempt, this otherwise worked flawlessly. The only minor drawback is the decryption password prompt showing for a few seconds at boot before the auto-unlock kicks in. The only major drawback is that it doesn’t bring the same security benefits as TPM-backed full disk encryption… Perhaps readers know of a better way, perhaps by enrolling a Secure Boot key before TPM locks it in?

What this leaves me with

No real fixes and a workaround: install with plain LUKS, and let oem-somerville-oddish-meta do its job on first boot. Will I feel like I achieved something, I still lost the security benefits that come with decrypting on user login, our clevis implementation is but a pale imitation of what TPM enables. This, or I had to enter my recovery key on every boot, defeating the purpose.

The real problem is the snap-managed kernel hiding behind a single checkbox with major consequences one may quickly forget about. Someone who doesn’t toggle third-party drivers on for any reason may never see the warning, then hit issues weeks or months later when those drivers may be wanted or needed. One installer was outputting two different operating systems.

Looking back, none of this was a surprise. When Canonical announced the feature, online communities immediately picked up on it. On LWN, user mfuzzey prophesied:

I suspect there is a significant subset of users who would like TPM based FDE for the security benefits but would prefer to stay with DEBs.

On Hacker News, the top comment by michaelt about Ubuntu’s blog post went further:

And there it is. I suppose having your kernel command line signed by Canonical and unmodifiable by the system owner without a pain-in-the-ass manual ‘machine owner key enrolment’ process is very much on-brand for Snap.

It only took me several hours to rediscover what these readers had warned about three years ago. I can accept Canonical restricting features behind their snap kernel, but I wish they had done a better job at informing users about their installer’s option. If you’re setting up a modern laptop with Ubuntu, know what choosing TPM-FDE actually means.

Dell Latitude 7450 configured with an Intel Core Ultra 7 165U CPU and Hynix HI-556 camera sensor.

sentences.zh: 相机位于快照侧的死胡同

blocks.html_en: Could I get the camera working anyway, staying on the snap kernel? The pre-built modules were there, so that left building them with DKMS. They built fine, but would not load:

sentences.en: Could I get the camera working anyway, staying on the snap kernel?
sentences.zh: 我能让相机继续工作，留在快照内核上吗？

sentences.en: The pre-built modules were there, so that left building them with DKMS.
sentences.zh: 预构建的模块已经存在，因此需要使用 DKMS 来构建它们。

sentences.en: They built fine, but would not load:
sentences.zh: 他们构建得很好，但无法加载：

blocks.html_en: Secure Boot, which TPM-FDE requires, refused unsigned modules. To sign my own I’d need to enroll a key, which changes PCR 7, which is what the TPM is using for decryption. I could recover from that with the recovery key, but the documentation is blunt about the side-effect: “On subsequent boots, you have to continue using your recovery key.” There’s no supported way to reconverge after that. On this kernel, I was hitting a dead end for the camera.

sentences.en: Secure Boot, which TPM-FDE requires, refused unsigned modules.
sentences.zh: TPM-FDE 要求的安全启动拒绝未签名的模块。

sentences.en: To sign my own I’d need to enroll a key, which changes PCR 7, which is what the TPM is using for decryption.
sentences.zh: 要签署我自己的密钥，我需要注册一个密钥，这会更改 PCR 7，这是 TPM 用于解密的密钥。

sentences.en: I could recover from that with the recovery key, but the documentation is blunt about the side-effect: “On subsequent boots, you have to continue using your recovery key.”
sentences.zh: 我可以使用恢复密钥来恢复，但文档对副作用直言不讳：“在后续启动时，您必须继续使用恢复密钥。”

sentences.en: There’s no supported way to reconverge after that.
sentences.zh: 此后没有支持的重新聚合方法。

sentences.en: On this kernel, I was hitting a dead end for the camera.
sentences.zh: 在这个内核上，我的相机陷入了死胡同。

blocks.html_en: I still didn’t know why the camera was missing in the first place, so I decided to reinstall without TPM encryption, giving me a chance to disable Secure Boot and try again.

sentences.en: I still didn’t know why the camera was missing in the first place, so I decided to reinstall without TPM encryption, giving me a chance to disable Secure Boot and try again.
sentences.zh: 我仍然不知道为什么相机丢失了，所以我决定在没有 TPM 加密的情况下重新安装，让我有机会禁用安全启动并重试。

blocks.html_en: Reinstalling: plot twist

sentences.en: Reinstalling: plot twist
sentences.zh: 重装：剧情反转

blocks.html_en: I reinstalled from the same ISO, this time choosing plain LUKS with a passphrase instead of TPM encryption. Then, before running any single command on my system, I checked the camera again:

sentences.en: I reinstalled from the same ISO, this time choosing plain LUKS with a passphrase instead of TPM encryption.
sentences.zh: 我从同一个 ISO 重新安装，这次选择带有密码的普通 LUKS，而不是 TPM 加密。

sentences.en: Then, before running any single command on my system, I checked the camera again:
sentences.zh: 然后，在我的系统上运行任何单个命令之前，我再次检查了相机：

blocks.html_en: Amazingly, the camera was working. cheese showed my face. I’d done nothing. What had changed?

sentences.en: Amazingly, the camera was working.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，相机居然能工作。

sentences.en: cheese showed my face.
sentences.zh: 奶酪露出了我的脸。

sentences.en: I’d done nothing.

sentences.en: What had changed?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么变化？

blocks.html_en: The first thing I noticed was the kernel. uname -r showed a plain deb HWE kernel, and boot-managed-by-snapd was gone. The snap kernel was gone, good job me! I felt like my dog when I congratulate him: he feels very happy, but I’m pretty sure he doesn’t always know what he’s done.

sentences.en: The first thing I noticed was the kernel.
sentences.zh: 我注意到的第一件事是内核。

sentences.en: uname -r showed a plain deb HWE kernel, and boot-managed-by-snapd was gone.
sentences.zh: uname -r 显示了一个普通的 deb HWE 内核，并且 boot-management-by-snapd 消失了。

sentences.en: The snap kernel was gone, good job me!
sentences.zh: 快照内核消失了，干得好！

sentences.en: I felt like my dog when I congratulate him: he feels very happy, but I’m pretty sure he doesn’t always know what he’s done.
sentences.zh: 当我祝贺他时，我感觉就像我的狗：他感到非常高兴，但我很确定他并不总是知道自己做了什么。

blocks.html_en: That sent me back to Canonical’s blog post about the TPM-FDE feature, which describes what the checkbox actually does: “TPM-backed FDE: this will install a classic desktop system that gets its kernel and bootloader assets from snaps. Non TPM-backed FDE: this will install an entirely deb-based classic desktop system.” So one checkbox silently chooses between two architecturally different operating systems. Ubuntu has decided, for better or worse, that TPM encryption requires their snap-managed kernel.

sentences.en: That sent me back to Canonical’s blog post about the TPM-FDE feature, which describes what the checkbox actually does: “TPM-backed FDE: this will install a classic desktop system that gets its kernel and bootloader assets from snaps.
sentences.zh: 这让我回到 Canonical 关于 TPM-FDE 功能的博客文章，其中描述了该复选框的实际用途：“TPM 支持的 FDE：这将安装一个经典的桌面系统，该系统从快照获取其内核和引导加载程序资产。

sentences.en: Non TPM-backed FDE: this will install an entirely deb-based classic desktop system.”
sentences.zh: 非 TPM 支持的 FDE：这将安装一个完全基于 deb 的经典桌面系统。”

sentences.en: So one checkbox silently chooses between two architecturally different operating systems.
sentences.zh: 因此，一个复选框会默默地在两个架构不同的操作系统之间进行选择。

sentences.en: Ubuntu has decided, for better or worse, that TPM encryption requires their snap-managed kernel.
sentences.zh: 无论好坏，Ubuntu 已经决定 TPM 加密需要其快照管理内核。

blocks.html_en: That single difference explained the working camera. On a deb system, oem-somerville-oddish-meta is more than a stub pointing to a remote archive: once it adds the Dell archive, apt finds a higher-versioned package of the same name inside that archive, and that one pulls the HWE kernel and the camera stack. So the entire Latitude 7450 hardware stack works out-of-the-box on 24.04, zero effort required. On snap, it can’t, because the Dell OEM package depends on the linux-image deb, nowhere to be found in a snap environment.

sentences.en: That single difference explained the working camera.
sentences.zh: 这个单一的差异解释了相机的工作原理。

sentences.en: On a deb system, oem-somerville-oddish-meta is more than a stub pointing to a remote archive: once it adds the Dell archive, apt finds a higher-versioned package of the same name inside that archive, and that one pulls the HWE kernel and the camera stack.
sentences.zh: 在 deb 系统上，oem-somerville-oddish-meta 不仅仅是指向远程存档的存根：一旦添加了 Dell 存档，apt 就会在该存档中找到同名的更高版本的软件包，并且该软件包会提取 HWE 内核和相机堆栈。

sentences.en: So the entire Latitude 7450 hardware stack works out-of-the-box on 24.04, zero effort required.
sentences.zh: 因此，整个 Latitude 7450 硬件堆栈在 24.04 上开箱即用，无需任何努力。

sentences.en: On snap, it can’t, because the Dell OEM package depends on the linux-image deb, nowhere to be found in a snap environment.
sentences.zh: 在 snap 上，它不能，因为 Dell OEM 软件包依赖于 linux-image deb，在 snap 环境中找不到。

blocks.html_en: Getting the TPM auto-unlock anyway, without snap

sentences.en: Getting the TPM auto-unlock anyway, without snap
sentences.zh: 无论如何，让 TPM 自动解锁，无需快照

blocks.html_en: I still wanted the laptop to unlock itself without snap’s arcane machinery. A systemd-cryptenroll route I found online looked right but didn’t work, because Ubuntu’s initramfs uses the older Debian cryptsetup wrapper that silently ignores the TPM option. Fortunately, one of my favorite Linux tools came to the rescue: clevis.

sentences.en: I still wanted the laptop to unlock itself without snap’s arcane machinery.
sentences.zh: 我仍然希望笔记本电脑能够在没有 snap 神秘机制的情况下自行解锁。

sentences.en: A systemd-cryptenroll route I found online looked right but didn’t work, because Ubuntu’s initramfs uses the older Debian cryptsetup wrapper that silently ignores the TPM option.
sentences.zh: 我在网上找到的一个 systemd-cryptenroll 路线看起来不错，但不起作用，因为 Ubuntu 的 initramfs 使用旧的 Debian cryptsetup 包装器，它默默地忽略了 TPM 选项。

sentences.en: Fortunately, one of my favorite Linux tools came to the rescue: clevis.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我最喜欢的 Linux 工具之一拯救了我：U 形夹。

blocks.html_en: While I had to wipe the first systemd-cryptenroll attempt, this otherwise worked flawlessly. The only minor drawback is the decryption password prompt showing for a few seconds at boot before the auto-unlock kicks in. The only major drawback is that it doesn’t bring the same security benefits as TPM-backed full disk encryption… Perhaps readers know of a better way, perhaps by enrolling a Secure Boot key before TPM locks it in?

sentences.en: While I had to wipe the first systemd-cryptenroll attempt, this otherwise worked flawlessly.
sentences.zh: 虽然我不得不擦除第一次 systemd-cryptenroll 尝试，但除此之外它工作得完美无缺。

sentences.en: The only minor drawback is the decryption password prompt showing for a few seconds at boot before the auto-unlock kicks in.
sentences.zh: 唯一的小缺点是在启动自动解锁之前，解密密码提示会显示几秒钟。

sentences.en: The only major drawback is that it doesn’t bring the same security benefits as TPM-backed full disk encryption…
sentences.zh: 唯一的主要缺点是它无法带来与 TPM 支持的全磁盘加密相同的安全优势……

sentences.en: Perhaps readers know of a better way, perhaps by enrolling a Secure Boot key before TPM locks it in?
sentences.zh: 也许读者知道更好的方法，也许是在 TPM 锁定安全启动密钥之前注册它？

blocks.html_en: What this leaves me with

sentences.zh: 这给我留下了什么

blocks.html_en: No real fixes and a workaround: install with plain LUKS, and let oem-somerville-oddish-meta do its job on first boot. Will I feel like I achieved something, I still lost the security benefits that come with decrypting on user login, our clevis implementation is but a pale imitation of what TPM enables. This, or I had to enter my recovery key on every boot, defeating the purpose.

sentences.zh: 没有真正的修复和解决方法：使用普通的 LUKS 安装，并让 oem-somerville-oddish-meta 在首次启动时完成其工作。

sentences.en: Will I feel like I achieved something, I still lost the security benefits that come with decrypting on user login, our clevis implementation is but a pale imitation of what TPM enables.
sentences.zh: 我是否会觉得自己取得了一些成就，但我仍然失去了用户登录解密带来的安全优势，我们的 U 形夹实现只是对 TPM 功能的苍白模仿。

sentences.zh: 否则我必须在每次启动时输入恢复密钥，从而达不到目的。

blocks.html_en: The real problem is the snap-managed kernel hiding behind a single checkbox with major consequences one may quickly forget about. Someone who doesn’t toggle third-party drivers on for any reason may never see the warning, then hit issues weeks or months later when those drivers may be wanted or needed. One installer was outputting two different operating systems.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR：在 Ubuntu 24.04 和 26.04 上重新发现这一点，在安装程序中勾选“使用硬件支持的磁盘加密”会默默地为您提供一个基于 snap 的系统（snap 内核和引导加载程序，如 Ubuntu Core），而不是普通的基于 deb 的系统。 在现代笔记本电脑上，这可能会破坏硬件支持（在我的例子中是网络摄像头），没有受支持的方法来修复它或具有等效的功能集。

我拿到了经过 Ubuntu 22.04 认证的 Dell Latitude 7450（这篇有关认证过程的 Ubuntu 博客文章值得一读），并决定尝试更新的 LTS 版本。 Ubuntu 26.04 已经发布，但确实很新，所以我决定从 24.04 开始。 我下载了 ISO，勾选了使用 TPM 的磁盘加密复选框（我必须为此禁用第三方驱动程序），然后发现系统中的摄像头无法工作。

过去，我从未在笔记本电脑上使用 Ubuntu 获得过完美的体验，但那些都是来自未经认证的机器。 Latitude 7450 得到了 Canonical 的加持，那么这是怎么回事呢？ 令人惊讶的是，使用相同的 ISO 重新安装并勾选不同的加密复选框（带有密码的 LVM）可以使相机开箱即用。

让我们试着弄清楚发生了什么。

在 vanilla 24.04 中发现该问题

最初，在我的 24.04 安装中，大多数都是开箱即用的。 Ubuntu 安装了一个元包 oem-somerville-oddish-meta （“Somerville”是 Dell 的 OEM 程序，“Oddish”是这台笔记本电脑的代号，是的，就像 Pokémon），将 Dell 的 apt 存档添加到我的源中，因此我对兼容性充满信心。 经验证，iGPU、Wi-Fi、音频、指纹识别器和 Thunderbolt 均正常工作。 戴尔构建 Latitude_7450_Latitude_7650_Ubuntu_2204_A01_Recovery_image.iso 22.04 的工作似乎已向上游转移，干得好！

除了…

相机坏了，没有办法修复它

网络摄像头是明显的遗漏，根本没有 /dev/video*。 硬件很好（笔记本电脑是新的，lsusb 显示了芯片）。 dkms status 将 IPU6 摄像头模块列为已注册但从未构建。 在互联网上搜索后，解决这个问题的方法是：安装戴尔存档中的预构建摄像头模块而不是 DKMS 模块，添加 v4l2-relayd，重新启动，完成。 令人惊讶的是，它没有安装：

$ sudo apt install linux-modules-ipu6-generic ...
 linux-modules-ipu6-6.8.0-111-generic : Depends: linux-image-6.8.0-111-generic but it is not going to be installed

这些模块需要附加一个内核映像。 好吧，让我们获取内核映像：

$ sudo apt install linux-image-6.8.0-111-generic linux-modules-ipu6-generic ...
 boot-managed-by-snapd : Conflicts: linux-image, grub-efi-amd64, grub-pc,
                                    linux-firmware, shim-signed ...

Oh no.

我的内核很快！

我愣住了，boot-management-by-snapd 是什么意思？ 我知道“启动”这个词，也知道“快照”这个词，但是快照管理的启动？ 它与 linux-image、GRUB、shim、linux-firmware 以及基于 Debian 的系统用于引导的所有内容发生冲突。

$ cat /proc/cmdline
snapd_recovery_mode=run console=tty1 ...
$ snap list | grep pc-kernel
pc-kernel   6.8.0-110.110   3374   24/stable   canonical✓   kernel
$ dpkg -l | grep linux-image
(no output)
$ ls /boot/efi
ls: cannot access '/boot/efi': No such file or directory

没有 deb 内核，没有 /boot/efi。 我的内核很简单，我不知道该怎么做。 经过一番研究，我了解了 Ubuntu Core，它实际上是一个非常酷的嵌入式设备不可变发行版，但这并不是我认为我为正常笔记本电脑使用而安装的发行版。 在安装了 Debian 和 Ubuntu 数十次之后，我不知道自己做了什么不同的事情。

相机位于快照侧的死胡同

我能让相机继续工作，留在快照内核上吗？ 预构建的模块已经存在，因此需要使用 DKMS 来构建它们。 他们构建得很好，但无法加载：

$ sudo modprobe intel_ipu6
modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'intel_ipu6': Key was rejected by service

TPM-FDE 要求的安全启动拒绝未签名的模块。 要签署我自己的密钥，我需要注册一个密钥，这会更改 PCR 7，这是 TPM 用于解密的密钥。 我可以使用恢复密钥来恢复，但文档对副作用直言不讳：“在后续启动时，您必须继续使用恢复密钥。” 此后没有支持的重新聚合方法。 在这个内核上，我的相机陷入了死胡同。

我仍然不知道为什么相机丢失了，所以我决定在没有 TPM 加密的情况下重新安装，让我有机会禁用安全启动并重试。

重装：剧情反转

我从同一个 ISO 重新安装，这次选择带有密码的普通 LUKS，而不是 TPM 加密。 然后，在我的系统上运行任何单个命令之前，我再次检查了相机：

$ ls /dev/video*
*49 entries*

令人惊奇的是，相机居然能工作。 奶酪露出了我的脸。 我什么也没做。 发生了什么变化？

我注意到的第一件事是内核。 uname -r 显示了一个普通的 deb HWE 内核，并且 boot-management-by-snapd 消失了。 快照内核消失了，干得好！ 当我祝贺他时，我感觉就像我的狗：他感到非常高兴，但我很确定他并不总是知道自己做了什么。

这让我回到 Canonical 关于 TPM-FDE 功能的博客文章，其中描述了该复选框的实际用途：“TPM 支持的 FDE：这将安装一个经典的桌面系统，该系统从快照获取其内核和引导加载程序资产。 非 TPM 支持的 FDE：这将安装一个完全基于 deb 的经典桌面系统。” 因此，一个复选框会默默地在两个架构不同的操作系统之间进行选择。 无论好坏，Ubuntu 已经决定 TPM 加密需要其快照管理内核。

这个单一的差异解释了相机的工作原理。 在 deb 系统上，oem-somerville-oddish-meta 不仅仅是指向远程存档的存根：一旦添加了 Dell 存档，apt 就会在该存档中找到同名的更高版本的软件包，并且该软件包会提取 HWE 内核和相机堆栈。 因此，整个 Latitude 7450 硬件堆栈在 24.04 上开箱即用，无需任何努力。 在 snap 上，它不能，因为 Dell OEM 软件包依赖于 linux-image deb，在 snap 环境中找不到。

无论如何，让 TPM 自动解锁，无需快照

我仍然希望笔记本电脑能够在没有 snap 神秘机制的情况下自行解锁。 我在网上找到的一个 systemd-cryptenroll 路线看起来不错，但不起作用，因为 Ubuntu 的 initramfs 使用旧的 Debian cryptsetup 包装器，它默默地忽略了 TPM 选项。 幸运的是，我最喜欢的 Linux 工具之一拯救了我：U 形夹。

sudo apt install clevis-luks clevis-tpm2 clevis-initramfs
sudo clevis luks bind -d /dev/nvme0n1p3 tpm2 '{"pcr_bank":"sha256","pcr_ids":"7"}'
sudo update-initramfs -u

虽然我不得不擦除第一次 systemd-cryptenroll 尝试，但除此之外它工作得完美无缺。 唯一的小缺点是在启动自动解锁之前，解密密码提示会显示几秒钟。 唯一的主要缺点是它无法带来与 TPM 支持的全磁盘加密相同的安全优势…… 也许读者知道更好的方法，也许是在 TPM 锁定安全启动密钥之前注册它？

这给我留下了什么

没有真正的修复和解决方法：使用普通的 LUKS 安装，并让 oem-somerville-oddish-meta 在首次启动时完成其工作。 我是否会觉得自己取得了一些成就，但我仍然失去了用户登录解密带来的安全优势，我们的 U 形夹实现只是对 TPM 功能的苍白模仿。 否则我必须在每次启动时输入恢复密钥，从而达不到目的。

真正的问题是快照管理的内核隐藏在单个复选框后面，其重大后果可能很快就会被忘记。 出于任何原因不打开第三方驱动程序的人可能永远不会看到警告，然后在几周或几个月后可能需要这些驱动程序时遇到问题。 一名安装程序输出了两个不同的操作系统。

回想起来，这一切并不令人意外。 当 Canonical 宣布该功能时，在线社区立即关注它。 在 LWN 上，用户 mfuzzey 预言：

我怀疑有很大一部分用户希望基于 TPM 的 FDE 获得安全优势，但更愿意继续使用 DEB。

在 Hacker News 上，michaelt 对 Ubuntu 博客文章的置顶评论更进一步：

就是这样。 我想，让你的内核命令行由 Canonical 签名并且系统所有者无法修改，而无需痛苦的手动“机器所有者密钥注册”过程，这对于 Snap 来说是非常符合品牌的。

我只花了几个小时就重新发现了这些读者三年前警告过的内容。 我可以接受他们的 snap 内核背后的 Canonical 限制功能，但我希望他们在告知用户安装程序的选项方面做得更好。 如果您正在使用 Ubuntu 设置现代笔记本电脑，请了解选择 TPM-FDE 的实际含义。

Dell Latitude 7450 配置了 Intel Core Ultra 7 165U CPU 和 Hynix HI-556 摄像头传感器。
